testsJudged: The new tests cover every way the tester tried to break it: stored topic and role message once with the lane on (TestAStoredTopicStillReachesAServingPortOnce), the rolling deploy (TestTwoListenersOnOneMachineDeliverALiveTopicOnce), the exception read-back, a mismatched or invalid envelope (TestALiveLaneDropsAnInvalidEnvelope), the refusing grant (TestAListenerWhoseGrantRefusesEveryTopicEndsItsStart and the natslive subtest), recovery (TestCoreSubOKReportsTheReplacementAfterTheClientReplacesAClosedConnection), healthz, SIGTERM, config parsing, the address rule and ValidHost. No red test was needed.
observations: Host check refuses a trailing-dot FQDN (host.example.) and any machine id with a space; envoy-client sends ENVOY_MACHINE_ID || os.hostname(), and the deploy convention sets ENVOY_MACHINE_ID to the hostname, so no realistic registration is refused (the implementer's open question).

The host check runs only on write: an entry an older listener wrote with an unchecked host is read as-is by a new listener of the same machine id during a rolling deploy until it ages out (5 min session TTL). A malformed host then fails its delivery or is caught by url parsing; not a failure of any criterion.
Building envoy-infra's CLI rewrites packages/envoy/infra/go.work.sum at base 064cc728 as at the head; pre-existing, not this PR's; the tester restored the file.
